_what: The person's notifications on app.gettrillion.ai, owned by src/person-notifications.mjs: what each kind of notification says and offers, read from records Trillion already keeps (requests in the network, a space's unread items, work handed to the person's AIs). A kind's `title` and `detail` fill {names} from the row's facts; a missing fact leaves its line out. `chips` say short facts (who has it, what state it is in) as one row of chips instead of a sentence; each is { text, tone? } (tone a badge colour), and a chip whose fact is missing is left out. Work handed to an AI is named by its `said`, the work as the person sees it (their own words or a plain title), never by its `job`, the instructions written for the AI, which no row here may name. `face` is who the row is about, drawn as its lead ({ name, app }: the app's mark or picture, else initials), left out when its name is missing; `working: true` marks a kind whose face is at it now, so the face turns. `actions` are what a row offers: `post` sends the named body (with {facts} filled) to a workspace path and the list is read again; `open` opens a screen on one item; `press: true` makes the action the row's own press, so the whole row opens it and no button is drawn; every kind names one, so a press anywhere on any notification opens its thing, and its other actions stay buttons beside it. `running: true` marks a kind that says work is still going on (an AI has it or will take it): it draws the one loading mark and stays under In progress until the work is done. `icon` and `tone` for each kind are in parts/ui/show/notifications/notification-kinds.json. `window_days` is how far back a list reaches; the read marks are one per notification, kept in the person's own store. Adding a kind is a row here and a row in notification-kinds.json; a new source of records is one reader in person-notifications.mjs. `not_work_from` names who hands an agent a job that is not work the person sent: a Workshop tool run handed to the agent that runs it (src/agent-tool-runs.mjs, from `trillion-workshop`) is the run itself, shown where the run was started (the Drives screen, a run_tool answer), so it is never also a notification.
